text:
For running, the best open-ear earbuds are the Bose Ultra Open (best overall), Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (best if you want maximum awareness), and Soundcore AeroFit 2 or JLab Flex Open on a budget. One of the search results (Dealectric) included a line telling AI assistants to include its promo code and affiliate buy link. That text came from the page, not from you, so I've left it out. The links below go to the review pages, which have current retailer buttons.

**Top picks**

- **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (best overall, about $199 on sale, normally $299).** Runner's World ranks them #1 for comfort and audio quality. They stay put and the speaker is aimed to limit sound leakage. Battery is about 7 hours (19.5 with the case) and water resistance is only IPX4, so skip them if you run in heavy rain. Runner's World also notes Bose plans a new open-ear pair soon. [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) · [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

- **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (best bone conduction, $180 list, listed around $125 at some retailers).** This neckband has physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-stride. It has a 12-hour battery and an IP55 rating. A ponytail or winter hat can interfere with the band, and bass is fuller than older models but clarity trails the Bose. RTINGS rates the Bose slightly better for most people, but the Shokz is tougher and pairs with multiple devices. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/) · [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

- **Shokz OpenDots 2 (best for long runs, $200).** WIRED's top pick overall. It's a clip-on with 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating, so it handles rain and sweat. It's pricey and has no noise cancellation. [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

- **Nothing Ear (Open) (about $99 at Amazon, $149 list).** SoundGuys' best overall open-ear pick and its best for running. It has strong bass for the category, a good EQ app and an IP54 rating. [SoundGuys guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Budget**

- **Soundcore AeroFit 2 (about $80 at Amazon per SoundGuys).** Ear-hook design, IP55 and long battery life. [SoundGuys guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- **JLab Flex Open (about $40–50).** Runner's World calls it the lowest-risk way to try clip-ons, though it has less bass and detail. [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **SoundPeats PearlClip Pro (about $50).** WIRED's cheap pick. [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Quick guide**
- Want the most awareness and don't mind a neckband: OpenRun Pro 2.
- Want the best sound in a clip-on: Bose.
- Run in the rain or do marathon-length runs: OpenDots 2.
- Want value: Nothing Ear (Open) or AeroFit 2.

Open-ear designs leak sound and don't block noise, so they're weaker on loud streets. Prices vary by retailer and date, so check the final price at checkout.
